title: kbtail.py prints the first line holding an IPv4 or a home path about 9 s late, while redaction loads the public kb's names
goal: kbtail.py prints a transcript line that holds a private IPv4 address and a home path within 2 seconds, both redacted, in `--once` and while following, from a fresh process

run:
import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading, time, uuid
R = os.getcwd(); T = tempfile.mkdtemp(); C = os.path.join(T, "cfg")
sid = str(uuid.uuid4())
pdir = os.path.join(C, "projects", "-planted-project"); os.makedirs(pdir)
P = os.path.join(pdir, sid + ".jsonl")
ip = ".".join(["10", "1", "2", "3"])
home = "/" + "Users" + "/" + "plantedname" + "/notes.txt"
def ent(text):
    return json.dumps({"type": "assistant", "cwd": T, "sessionId": sid, "timestamp": "2026-10-26T10:00:00Z",
                       "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": text}]}}) + "\n"
with open(P, "w") as f:
    f.write(ent("planted-plain-line"))
env = dict(os.environ, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=C, COLUMNS="200", KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(T, "coord.sqlite"))
problems = []
with open(os.path.join(T, "once.jsonl"), "w") as f:
    f.write(ent("planted-once-line host " + ip + " file " + home))
t0 = time.monotonic()
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "_tools/kbtail.py", "--once", os.path.join(T, "once.jsonl")], cwd=R, env=env,
                   capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
took = time.monotonic() - t0
if r.returncode != 0 or "planted-once-line" not in r.stdout:
    problems.append("--once exit %d: %s" % (r.returncode, r.stderr[-300:]))
if took > 2.0:
    problems.append("--once on a line with an IPv4 and a home path took %.1f s (limit 2 s)" % took)
if ip in r.stdout or "plantedname" in r.stdout:
    problems.append("--once shows the IPv4 or the home path's user name")
p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "_tools/kbtail.py", P], cwd=R, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
lines = []
threading.Thread(target=lambda: [lines.append((time.monotonic(), x)) for x in p.stdout], daemon=True).start()
end = time.monotonic() + 10
while time.monotonic() < end and not any("planted-plain-line" in x for _, x in lines):
    time.sleep(0.05)
with open(P, "a") as f:
    f.write(ent("planted-live-line host " + ip + " file " + home))
t1 = time.monotonic()
end = t1 + 10
while time.monotonic() < end and not any("planted-live-line" in x for _, x in lines):
    time.sleep(0.05)
hit = [t for t, x in lines if "planted-live-line" in x]
if not hit or hit[0] - t1 > 2.0:
    problems.append("the appended line with an IPv4 and a home path printed %s after its write (limit 2 s)" %
                    ("%.1f s" % (hit[0] - t1) if hit else "not within 10 s"))
if any(ip in x or "plantedname" in x for _, x in lines):
    problems.append("the follow shows the IPv4 or the home path's user name")
p.terminate()
try:
    p.wait(5)
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    p.kill()
print("\n".join(problems) or "ok (--once %.2f s)" % took)
sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)

notes: Found by the fresh review of SP-wurbmsid (S2 there; the operator raised it to S1 on 2026-10-26). Cause: the first text that needs the public root's names (an IPv4, a /Users/<name> path, probably a host) makes redact.redact load them through mon_view.LazyKnown, about 9 s of full CPU once per process, and the follow loop is blocked meanwhile. A display may redact more than the query log does: over-redaction is acceptable here, a leak is not. Every displayed string still passes redaction and the leak scan. _tools/redact.py is held by another sprint's item (BG-6gpjcsg6): a fix that needs it stops with a gate.
